decisions.reason: False positive: F2 explicitly cites proof step 2.1 of lem-schwartz-cutoffs-from-the-standard-smooth-step. That step constructs a(t)/(a(t)+a(1-t)), proves smoothness and its constant regions; step 1.1 proves all derivatives of a vanish at zero. These establish the stated theta and endpoint flatness despite the narrower radial-cutoff Statement. The boundary-strip Taylor estimate with N>M and rational polynomial approximation give a countable dense set; no Choice is needed.

The cited translation theorem does not establish nullity under reflection. Step 1.1 also incorrectly infers a global null set x-D_sigma from the local C=closure(D_sigma) intersect J. Added the existing linear-change-of-variables theorem for t -> -t (absolute determinant one), then translated -C and applied completeness only to the integrand discontinuities inside (x-D_sigma) intersect [-R,R], which lie in x-C. This repairs the missing dependency and local/global inference without changing the Statement.

The original title claimed failure to approximate even targets without excluding constants, but width zero realizes every constant. The actual Statement refuted and three-step proof are sound: sine oddness gives S(0)=c and (S(1)+S(-1))/2=c, forcing max(|c|,|c-1|)>=1/2 against x^2. Changed only the title to the square-function obstruction; this is a nonfatal title defect, not a density-proof defect.

Library def-natural-numbers explicitly has 0 in N, so the displayed witness sigma and spike sets included the undefined reciprocal 1/0. Restricted all spike indices to n in N with n>=1, making the activation well-defined without altering the refuted Statement. Also absorbed constant affine units into the output bias before isolating divergent spikes, so the assertion that all other spike contributions eventually vanish applies precisely to nonconstant units; nonpolynomiality is established at step 2.1 rather than announced as already proved in step 1.1. Fatal classification concerns the originally undefined counterexample witness.
